strengths: The paper addresses a worthwhile problem: predicting human response times under changing external stimuli. Combining task-trained neural representations with a policy-controlled evidence accumulator is a well-motivated approach that could provide useful cognitive structure.

The two-day experiment compares four stimulus schedules, with 36 retained participants. Evaluation across general, group, individual, and leave-one-participant-out settings provides useful perspectives on personalization and participant generalization.

The reported aggregate results consistently favor the hybrid agent over Pure DRL. MAPE decreases from 0.3034 to 0.2999 in the general setting and from 0.3037 to 0.2905 under LOPO. Feature comparisons support the arithmetic representation, and the reported training times of 4.42 versus 38.30 minutes suggest a potentially useful efficiency benefit.
weaknesses: Essential methodological information is missing from the supplied manuscript. Referenced Appendices S2–S6 are absent, leaving the RL algorithm and reward, DDM dynamics and parameter construction, optimization settings, and adaptive stimulus rule insufficiently specified. Code and data availability are only promised. These omissions prevent reproduction and assessment of whether the implemented objective supports the principal claims.

The claimed explanation of cognition at individual stimulus frames is not established by response-time prediction. Many latent action trajectories can produce the same threshold-crossing time. The plotted trajectories therefore describe the fitted controller without demonstrating that participants use the inferred accumulation process. Nonzero inferred effects in the no-pressure group could also reflect correction of baseline prediction errors. Model-recovery experiments or controlled changes to within-trial stimulus timing would provide stronger evidence.

The main comparison does not isolate the contribution of the DDM. Pure DRL processes the whole stimulus and produces one adjustment, whereas the hybrid model processes sequential frames and actions. Temporal representation and decision structure therefore change together. A sequential neural baseline without the DDM, a stimulus-aware supervised predictor, and a fitted diffusion model with stimulus covariates are needed to establish the value of the proposed combination.

The predictive improvements are modest, and their reliability is unclear. The paper provides no uncertainty estimates or paired participant-level analysis for the MAPE differences, nor adequately documented repeated-seed results. The runtime comparison also lacks an operational convergence criterion and variability estimates. The evidence supports promising point estimates more strongly than robust superiority.

The evaluation pipeline is insufficiently documented. It is unclear which no-pressure observations train the baseline SVM and whether normalization, SVM fitting, and model selection occur entirely within each LOPO training fold. This leaves leakage risks unresolved rather than demonstrating leakage. Shuffled within-participant splits also assess interpolation across the study, not prospective prediction of later behavior.

Some behavioral conclusions exceed the statistical evidence. The reported significant response-time contrast is random versus none; this does not establish that random pressure outperforms every alternative. Likewise, nonsignificant accuracy differences do not establish that pressure leaves accuracy unaffected. With only 7–10 retained participants per group and unspecified criteria for excluding extreme outliers, sensitivity analyses would materially strengthen these conclusions.

Positioning against prior work needs greater precision. The suggestion that DDMs primarily support posterior estimation rather than future prediction is misleading: fitted generative diffusion models can make out-of-sample predictions. Although prior cognitive–neural and RL–DDM combinations are cited, the paper does not convincingly establish what additional predictive or explanatory capability its construction provides beyond those approaches.
